title: A breakpoint by hand
description:
Model how a software breakpoint works: put `0xCC` in the code, and put the byte back after it hits.

```
code:  48 83 EC 28 E8 ...
set breakpoint at 0x4 -> saved E8, wrote CC
hit at 0x4: restore E8, rewind rip to 0x4, single-step, write CC again
remove -> E8 back, nothing left changed
```
hints: Reading memory through a debugger must hide your own `0xCC`s, or a disassembly view shows nonsense (lesson 3.01).
Re-arming after the single step is what lets the breakpoint hit again on the next loop.
requirements: A breakpoint table from address to the original byte.
Setting twice at one address is refused; removing restores exactly the original.
After a hit, the instruction pointer goes back by 1 (the `int3` already ran).
stretch: Model hardware breakpoints: four address slots and no change to the code.
